title: Adjective Agreement 4: Spelling Rule Effects
description: The mechanism behind Lesson 3's mixed-looking forms. Three spelling rules cover almost every surface oddity: no -ы after velar / husher, no unstressed -о after husher, stressed masculine -ой instead of -ый.
descriptionRussian: Механизм урока 3: после к/г/х и ж/ш/ч/щ нельзя писать -ы (только -и); после шипящих в безударной позиции нельзя писать -о (только -е); ударное окончание мужского рода — -ой вместо -ый.
intro: One of the three rules in this lesson you have already met, back in the noun book, deciding plurals. It turns up here doing the same job on adjective endings, and it will keep turning up for as long as you study Russian. That is the thing worth noticing today: the language runs on a small number of spelling rules that cut across every part of speech. Pay for them once and they keep refunding you.
rules: Rule 1: After к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ Russian never writes -ы. Where the regular ending would be -ы, write -и instead. This produces all the -ие plural forms in the mixed-stem class (маленькие, русские, хорошие, большие) and the -ий masculine forms (хороший, маленький, русский).
Rule 2: After ж, ш, ч, щ, ц in unstressed position Russian writes -е, not -о. So хорошее, свежее. When the ending is stressed, the original -о stays: большо́е, чужо́е.
Rule 3: Stressed masculine adjective endings are written -ой, not -ый. молодо́й, дорого́й, плохо́й, большо́й. The other forms of the same adjectives keep regular endings (-ая, -ое, -ые / -ие).
The three rules cover every surface oddity from Lesson 3. Once you know which rule is firing, you can predict the form rather than memorize it.
examples: В Москве большие парки. (Moscow has big parks.) Rule 1 fires: больш- ends in the husher -ш-, so the plural is -ие not -ые.
Это дорогой магазин. (This is an expensive store.) Rule 3 fires: the ending is stressed (дорого́й), so the masculine form is -ой not -ый.
Это русские учителя. (These are Russian teachers.) Rule 1 fires: русск- ends in the velar -к-, so the plural is -ие not -ые.
У Маши свежее молоко. (Masha has fresh milk.) Rule 2 fires: свеж- ends in the husher -ж- and the ending is unstressed, so the neuter is -ее not -ое.
Молодой человек гуляет в парке. (A young man is walking in the park.) Rule 3 fires: молодо́й is end-stressed, so the masculine form is -ой.

Compare хоро́шее (Rule 2: husher + unstressed → -ее) with большо́е (no rule fires here: the stress sits on the ending, so the -о survives). Same -ое slot in the paradigm; different stresses give different spellings.

rows.label: Rule 1

items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 3. День is masculine singular: which mixed-stem form fits?
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 3: the masculine form of хороший is хороший. Rule 1 (today): after the husher -ш-, the masculine ending is written -ий, not -ый. The Lesson 3 surface form falls out of the Rule 1 mechanism.

items.hint: Парки is plural. The plural ending after the husher -ш- is shaped by Rule 1.
items.explanation: Парки is plural. Rule 1 says no -ы after the husher -ш-: the regular plural -ые is replaced with -ие, giving большие. The same rule turns хорошые into хорошие and маленькые into маленькие.

items.hint: Магазин is masculine singular. The adjective дорого́й is end-stressed.
items.explanation: Магазин is masculine singular. The adjective is end-stressed (дорого́й), so Rule 3 applies: the masculine ending is written -ой not -ый. Compare новый (stem-stressed) which keeps -ый. Same masculine slot, different stress, different spelling.

items.hint: Учителя is plural. Which spelling rule fires after -к-?
items.explanation: Учителя is plural. Rule 1 fires after -к-: no -ы, so the plural is русские, not 'русскые'. The same rule works on every plural form of an adjective whose stem ends in к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, or щ.

items.hint: Молоко is neuter singular. Свеж- ends in a husher and the ending is unstressed.
items.explanation: Молоко is neuter singular. Rule 2 fires: the husher -ж- plus an unstressed ending forces -е, not -о. So свежее, not 'свежое'. Compare большо́е (stressed -о́е), where the rule does not fire because the stress sits on the ending.

items.promptEnglish: A young man is walking in the park.
items.hint: Человек is masculine singular. Молодо́й is end-stressed.
items.explanation: Человек is masculine singular. The adjective is end-stressed (молодо́й), so Rule 3 applies: the masculine ending is written -ой, not -ый.

blanks: На улице _____ дома. (There are small houses on the street.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Дома is plural. Rule 1 fires after -к-: the plural ending is written -ие, not -ые. So маленькие, never 'маленькые'.

minimalPairs.explanation: Магазин is masculine singular. End-stressed adjective takes -ой (Rule 3): дорогой. Дорогая would require a feminine noun like дорогая машина.
Книги is plural. After the husher -ш-, the plural ending is -ие (Rule 1): хорошие. Хорошая is the feminine singular and would require one specific feminine noun.

errorCorrection.sentence: На улице маленькые дома уже сто лет.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There have been small houses on this street for a hundred years now.
errorCorrection.explanation: After -к-, Rule 1 forbids -ы in writing. The plural ending must switch to -ие: маленькие. Маленькые is invalid Russian spelling, exactly the trap the rule blocks.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Маши хорошое настроение сегодня утром.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is in a good mood this morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: After the husher -ш with an UNSTRESSED ending, Rule 2 forbids -о in writing. The neuter ending switches to -ее: хорошее. Compare with большо́е (neuter of большой) where the ending IS stressed; Rule 2 only fires when the ending is unstressed. The husher decides the writing; the stress decides whether the rule applies.

errorCorrection.sentence: Молодый человек гуляет в парке с собакой.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: A young man is walking in the park with a dog.
errorCorrection.explanation: Молодо́й is end-stressed. Rule 3: stressed masculine ending is written -ой, not -ый. So молодой. The same group of stressed-ending adjectives includes большой, другой, золотой, all of which share the -ой masculine ending. Unstressed adjectives (новый, умный) keep -ый.

errorCorrection.sentence: В библиотеке английскые книги на третьей полке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are English books on the third shelf in the library.
errorCorrection.explanation: After -к, Rule 1 forbids -ы in writing. The plural ending switches to -ие: английские. Английскые is invalid Russian spelling - the same rule that fires in русские and маленькие.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это маленькые окна в детской комнате.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These are small windows in the children's room.
errorCorrection.explanation: The stem маленьк- ends in -к. Rule 1 (no -ы after к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч) blocks -ые in the plural; the ending switches to -ие: маленькие. Маленькые is invalid Russian spelling.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня есть хорошые друзья в Москве.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have good friends in Moscow.
errorCorrection.explanation: The stem хорош- ends in the husher -ш. Rule 1 forbids -ы after a husher, so the plural ending is spelled -ие: хорошие. Хорошые is invalid Russian spelling, exactly the trap the rule exists to catch.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша покупает свежый хлеб каждое утро в пекарне.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha buys fresh bread every morning at the bakery.
errorCorrection.explanation: The stem свеж- ends in the husher -ж. Rule 1 (no -ы after husher) blocks -ый; the masculine ending switches to -ий: свежий. Свежый is invalid Russian spelling. The same -ий switch fires on хороший (after -ш), нищий (after -щ), and any adjective with a husher-final stem.

reviewVocab.definition: spelling, orthography (how a word is written; in Russian adjective endings, three rules cover the surface variations from the basic agreement pattern)
reviewVocab.example: Правописание прилагательного 'большой' определяется ударением: ударное окончание пишется -ой, а не -ый.

reviewVocab.definition: the -ы / -и rule (Russian never writes -ы after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ; -и is written instead)
reviewVocab.example: По правилу -ы / -и форма 'маленькые дома' невозможна: правильно — 'маленькие дома'.

reviewVocab.definition: stressed ending (an ending that carries the word's stress; in masculine adjectives, a stressed ending is written -ой, an unstressed ending is written -ый)
reviewVocab.example: У слова 'молодой' ударное окончание -ой; у слова 'новый' окончание безударное и пишется -ый.
